description: Overhead-line conductor table for woof energy rating (IEEE 738-2012 steady-state thermal rating and Makkonen icing). Resistances are per subconductor, in ohm per metre, at 25 and 75 degC. height_m is the above-ground height the weather is read at; forecast heights are interpolated to it. subconductors is the number of subconductors per phase bundle; rating_amps is reported per phase bundle.
notes: ACSR Drake is the IEEE 738-2012 Annex B worked-example conductor; its values are the AC resistances printed there.

The GB conductors carry DC resistance at 20 degC from manufacturer tables citing BS 215-2 (ACSR) and BS EN 50182 (AAAC, AL5 alloy). They are carried to 25 and 75 degC with R(T) = R20 (1 + a20 (T - 20)), a20 = 0.00403 /K for hard-drawn aluminium (ACSR) and 0.0036 /K for aluminium alloy (AAAC). No AC/DC skin-effect factor is applied; for these sizes it is about 1 to 3 percent, so ratings are optimistic by about half that.

max_temp_c for the GB conductors is an assumed 75 degC design temperature, typical of legacy GB overhead-line design. Many circuits are designed to 50 degC or uprated to 90 degC; set the value for the circuit you rate.
emissivity 0.8 and absorptivity 0.8 follow the CIGRE TB 601 recommendation when the surface condition is unknown, and match the IEEE 738 Annex B example.
height_m defaults to 10 m. Real conductor clearance at mid-span on 132-400 kV lines is typically 7-25 m; raise it per entry if you know the circuit.

sources.ieee738: IEEE Std 738-2012, IEEE Standard for Calculating the Current-Temperature Relationship of Bare Overhead Conductors, Annex B (795 kcmil 26/7 ACSR Drake example).
sources.bs215: BS 215-2 ACSR conductor table as reproduced in manufacturer catalogues (Gulf Cables and Lumino Industries BS 215 tables): Lynx 30/7 x 2.79 mm, 19.53 mm, 0.1576 ohm/km at 20 degC; Zebra 54/7 x 3.18 mm, 28.62 mm, 0.0674 ohm/km at 20 degC.
sources.en50182: BS EN 50182 AL5 AAAC table as reproduced in manufacturer catalogues (Lumino Industries 'TYPE AL5 EN 50182'; Moseroth AAAC AL5): Upas 37/3.53 mm, 24.7 mm, 0.0879 ohm/km; Rubus 61/3.50 mm, 31.5 mm, 0.0544 ohm/km; Araucaria 61/4.14 mm, 37.3 mm, 0.0389 ohm/km, all at 20 degC.
sources.cigre601: CIGRE Technical Brochure 601 (2014), Guide for thermal rating calculations of overhead lines.

auto.description: --conductor auto picks an entry by the site's voltage_kv: the first rule whose min_kv the voltage reaches. Sites below the last rule, or with unknown voltage, get no rating (NaN) because distribution conductors vary too widely to guess.

rules.why: GB 400 kV: twin 700 mm2 AAAC Araucaria is the common modern bundle
GB 275 kV: twin 500 mm2 AAAC Rubus
GB 132 kV: single ACSR Lynx is the most widespread conductor; AAAC Upas is used on newer rebuilds, choose aaac_upas explicitly if known
